title: Mobile dental visits to care homes and private homes
audience: Assistants and service staff who travel with mobile dental teams to residential care, private homes or hospital beds.
learningOutcomes: Describe how instruments and materials are carried to and from a mobile visit.
Separate waste and sharps during a visit and carry them back to the practice.
Prepare an impression for transport so it is safe to handle.

instruction.heading: Why home and care visits differ
instruction.body: Dental care given in a residential care facility, a home or a hospital bed takes place away from the fixed surgery. Facilities there are often limited, and water, power and waste collection can be hard to arrange. The source applies the same standard precautions as in the surgery and expects staff to carry the protective equipment they need.

instruction.heading: Carrying instruments and materials
instruction.body: Clean instruments and materials travel in a lidded box of metal or stiff plastic so they are not damaged or spilled. Used instruments return to the practice inside a sealed, hard-walled box. Where possible they are cleaned during the visit using detergent solution, or misted with a product that keeps debris from hardening, before they travel. Impressions and try-ins travel in sealed plastic boxes, and impressions are rinsed to clear visible blood and spit before they reach the laboratory.

instruction.heading: Waste on the road
instruction.body: Waste is separated where it is generated. General waste goes into the facility's general waste. Sharp items and clinical waste follow the state rules, and a sharps container labelled to the Australian standard travels with the team back to the practice. Clinical waste is never left in the facility's general bin.

instruction.heading: Your part on the visit
instruction.body: The assistant carries the containers and waste bags, checks every seal and lid before leaving the room, and notes any missing supplies or facility problems for the practice. The assistant does not leave used items in the facility's rooms or bins.

procedure: Pack clean instruments in a lidded metal or stiff plastic box before you leave the practice.
Clean used instruments during the visit as far as the setting allows, then seal them in a hard-walled box.
Rinse impressions to clear visible blood and spit, then seal them in plastic.
Sort general waste, sharp items and clinical waste right where the work happened, by the bed or chair.
Check every seal and lid before you leave the room.
Return to the practice and move the waste to the store for collection.

workedExamples.situation: During a visit to a care home bedroom, the sharps container is nearly full and no basin is nearby.
workedExamples.reasoning: Seal the container at the level it is designed for, label it, and carry it back to the practice under the state rule. Do not empty it into the facility's bin or leave it open.

workedExamples.situation: A used impression with visible saliva must go to the laboratory from a home visit.
workedExamples.reasoning: Rinse off the visible saliva and blood first, then seal the impression in a plastic box. Label it and carry it so it does not get crushed.

equipmentAndPpe: Lidded metal or stiff plastic box for clean items
Sealed, hard-walled box for used items
Sharps container labelled to the applicable standard
Gloves and protective clothing for the visit

commonErrors.error: Carrying used instruments loose in a bag.
Putting sharps into the care home's general bin.
commonErrors.prevention: Carry the sharps back under the state rule.

commonErrors.error: Sealing an impression that still has visible saliva on it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The source is a general reference.
A visit does not lower the requirement for standard precautions. Staff carry their own protective equipment.
Sharp items and clinical waste leaving the visit are handed to the person responsible for collection. This lesson does not grant a licence to transport clinical waste.
The source names Australian standards and state rules.

qualityStandard: All used instruments leave the visit sealed.
Sharp items and clinical waste leave the visit in labelled containers.
documentationEvidence: Visit record listing the items taken out and the items returned
summary: Mobile visits follow the same standard precautions as the surgery, with more carrying.
Used instruments and sharps travel sealed, and waste is never left in facility bins.
Impressions are rinsed before they are sealed for transport.

knowledgeChecks.question: A mobile visit has used instruments that must go back to the practice. Which container is correct?
options: A plastic bag tied at the top.
An open tray on the car seat.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where does general waste from a care home visit go?
options: Into the sharps container in the car.
Into the kitchen sink and drain.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen to an impression before it is transported?
options: Rinse off visible blood and saliva, then seal it in plastic.
Carry it open in a tray, so the impression can air-dry on the way
Dry it in direct sunlight on the car dashboard for an hour.
Place it in a patient's drinking cup for the drive home.

sourceReferences: ADA Guidelines for Infection Control, 3rd ed. (Australian Dental Association, 2015), section F.13 (nursing home visits) and the note on transporting impressions and instruments; rights: user-held; reworded (no copying)

Cross-checked against HCG-17 (sharps) and HCG-18 (clinical waste). The source's general advice on waste is applied as a principle only. Source priority: the Australian NHMRC guideline, as summarised in HCG-01 to HCG-20, governs where it conflicts with this source.
